content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through working with element position with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns .offset() into a repeatable implementation choice. jQuery can read dimensions, positioning, scroll offsets, and computed CSS. Prefer classes and responsive CSS for presentation state, and avoid mixing layout reads with repeated writes.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
